title: Where the Compton edge comes from
caption: A 662 keV photon that scatters through angle θ hands the electron less than all its energy; the most is at θ = 180°, a backscatter. With 2E/m_ec² = 2.59, that maximum is 478 keV, the Compton edge: the Compton continuum in a scintillator spectrum stops there, short of the photopeak at 662 keV.
alt: Electron recoil energy against photon scattering angle for 662 keV gamma rays, rising from zero at 0 degrees to 478 keV at 180 degrees, below the 662 keV photon energy line.
description: Electron recoil energy T = E·ε(1 − cos θ)/(1 + ε(1 − cos θ)), with ε = E/m_ec² = 662/511.
Smaller scattering angles give smaller recoil energies, filling the continuum below the edge.
The photopeak, full absorption at 662 keV, lies above the edge.

checks.name: the largest recoil energy is the backscatter
